The standard PS5, on the other hand, is really starting to show its technical limitations: no VRR below 30 FPS, no Dolby Vision, and a weaker CPU. That makes a noticeable difference in action-heavy scenes and frame rates, since those situations put more strain on the processor.

OLED amplifies that lower frame rate, whereas LCDs slightly blurring between frames with "sample-and-hold" smooths the transitions. The thing that is bad at high frame rates, becomes a benefit at low frame rates.

Welcome to our GTA 6 guide, the latest game in Rockstar's long-running crime sandbox series. The goal of our guide is to help you get the most out of your time in Leonida, and achieve 100% completion with as few spoilers as possible.

This page serves as an index, and can be used as an easily browsable hub to access all of our specific guides pages, whether you're looking for collectibles or simply searching for gameplay tips.

Due to the unprecedented scale of GTA 6, this guide is a work in progress. We'll be updating daily after release with new discoveries, collectibles, and more. Each page includes a progress tracker so you can see at a glance how much work has been done. Thank you for your patience while we continue to explore Leonida alongside the rest of you.

On this page: GTA 6 Guide: All Guides & Collectibles

In our GTA 6 Trophy guide and roadmap, we'll explain how to unlock all 55 Trophies, with supporting information on collectibles and more to ensure you earn that Platinum as efficiently as possible.

If you're looking to achieve 100% completion in GTA 6, then our checklist outlines all of the requirements and what you need to do, with plenty of references to supporting guides to help you in your pursuit.

Our guide to GTA 6's missions will help you plot your way through the game's epic campaign, while making sure you don't miss out on any of the open world release's harder-to-find side-quests.

GTA 6 is bursting at the seams with secrets to discover, and our collectibles guide will help direct you to all of the important locations, with checklists so you can keep track of everything you've discovered so far.

GTA 6 may feature an epic crime story, but everyone needs a little downtime. In this section of our guide, we'll focus on some of the activities you experience while exploring the vast world of Leonida.

With a game as dense as GTA 6, you'll want to make sure you know all its secrets. In this part of our guide, we've included tips, tricks, and explanations of how important mechanics work.

#4103. Tripwire Interactive says it's laying off 36 staff in a "necessary" decision, while reassuring that Killing Floor 3 and Maneater 2 are still in active development

In a statement posted yesterday, Killing Floor developers Tripwire Interactive have announced that the studio is laying off 36 "talented" internal staff as part of a "workforce reduction". The job cuts come 16 months after the release of Killing Floor 3 (which James didn't care for), and within hours of unrelated yet equally dispiriting redunancies at Skydance Games.

Tripwire's announcement claims that this was "not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organisation," adding that "these are truly great people who are exceptional at their roles, and we will help support these individuals with compassion and dignity during this transition." There's a small hope in me that this might mean helping those affected find new jobs quickly, though it's hard to stay optimistic when mass layoffs in games development have become such a regular occurrence.

Despite this post primarily being about the loss of 36 livelihoods, Tripwire are quick to reassure fans that Killing Floor 3's post-launch updates remain in active development, as does their comedy shark-action sequel Maneater 2. The studio "remain committed to our awesome community", they say; apparently just not to their awesome employees.

This news also arrives just days after Tripwire expanded its publishing business to support small indie developers, and less than a year after its last round of layoffs in March. Tripwire also happens to have been acquired by layoff extraordinaire corporation Embracer in 2022, just for some relevant context.

#4102. "A fight for all workers": SAG-AFTRA throw weight behind emerging Rockstar union ahead of its GTA 6 release week vote

In what has come to feel like the dawn of the final day before Grand Theft Auto VI's release, one thing that Rockstar really don't want people to be aware of is the ongoing legal dispute between the Rockstar Games Workers Union and the studio itself following Rockstar's alleged union busting in firing 31 union members last year. Starting on the 12th through to the 26th, recognition of the union will be voted upon by staff to ensure that workers would be given a say over "topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies."

If it passes, the vote would also make the union the largest recognised union in the UK games industry, partly thanks to its partnership with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain. Now, the global labor union SAG-AFTRA have chimed in to endorse the Workers Union, offering solidarity to the members involved and granting important leverage from a global force.

SAG-AFTRA's statement declares that "unionisation is vital for the future of the video game industry", and that "in the face of record layoffs, job instability, hostile work places, and toxic crunch culture, it is now more critical than ever for unions and workers to stand in support of one another." They advocate for fair treatment, especially in the wake of displacement due to corporate mismanagement and genAI, and proudly state that "this is a fight for all workers."

Their statement closes by saying that "the gaming industry is a commercial juggernaut, and the people that create these amazing works of art deserve fair treatment and the opportunity to improve the terms of their employment with a strong voice at the bargaining table. We honor the courage of our fellow game workers at Rockstar and proudly support their union vote."

Solidarity with the workers, always. We can only wait and see how the voting process pans out.

#4099. In a reveal that might worry eventual PC players glancing at their GPUs, GTA 6 will target 30fps on all consoles

Oh, and and it'll be streamable on the Xbox One before it's playable on PC

In a press release coinciding with Grand Theft Auto VI becoming available for pre-load ahead of its November 19th release date, Rockstar has confirmed that the game "has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits." Read between the lines, and you can kind of make out the words "...so hope your PCs are up to spec, computer nerds."

GTA 6, of course, still does not have a confirmed PC version, even if Rockstar's former tech director says it's probably not far off. And despite this, even ancient, last-gen consoles are getting in on it, as the release also unexpectedly confirms that the game will be playable on Xbox One via Xbox Cloud Gaming, Microsoft's game streaming service that has suddenly lost its ability to work on PC. Granted, this comes with a warning: "as with all cloud streaming, connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay." If you ended up getting a PS4 last generation, no cloud play for you either, I'm afraid. It also states that it will "play best on Playstation 5 consoles", making great use of that Sony partnership, and will include Playstation Spectral Super Resolution and ray-traced shadows on PS5 Pro.

A 2026 current-gen game targeting 30fps, let alone one as titanic of a release as GTA VI, is probably not going to go down well with a lot of people, even if console players are traditionally les sensitive about FPS counts than PC players. What this does imply, though, is that the inevitable PC release might be an even more demanding behemoth than expected, if Xbox Series and PS5 versions can't even target 60fps. The availability of the game on Xbox One, even if just through cloud streaming, could have resulted in an acceptance that 60fps just wasn't going to be possible if it was also going to be able to 'run' on last-gen hardware. Either way, when it does eventually escape console exclusivity, hopefully trying to run GTA VI on anything less than an RTX 5080 won't set your PC on fire. Now, let me just quickly have a glance at GPU prices. Oh, no.

#4098. GTA 6's Mandy 'Is a Lot of Fun' Says Real-Life Actress as PS5 Players Are Smitten

I knew when I was reviewing GTA 6 that bunny boiler Mandy was going to take social media by storm, and it was quite fun watching the web react to Chapter 1’s ‘Pipeworks’ mission as the game launched overnight.

Now it’s being played by millions, actress Lexie Shoaibi has revealed she stars as the character, who not-so subtly throws herself at Jason during a very early story mission.

I actually think this is one example of the game’s slightly more mature writing. Wait, don’t roll your eyes – just hear me out, okay?

While this whole quest is played more for laughs, it’s there to establish the strength of Jason and Lucia’s relationship, as Jason shows no signs of being tempted by Mandy’s advances.

“She’s a lot of fun,” Shoaibi said, after confirming she did voice acting and motion capture for the character. At the time of writing, her post on Instagram has received over 90k likes.

But the response on social media would suggest gamers think she’s more than a “lot of fun”.

One post by Complex, featuring a few images and the caption ‘Mandy from GTA 6’, attracted 37 million views in just a few hours. Pertinently, it’s been bookmarked 54k times.

I don’t want to analyse this character too deeply, but I think it’s the moment I realised Rockstar has really pushed the boat out here.

The sheer variety of body types, and the detail invested into them, is unprecedented really. Mandy is just one of many similarly realistic NPCs in the game.

And while the character is almost certainly a psychopath, it’s been amusing to see her go viral overnight.

#4097. New Official Fallout-Inspired Game Announced, And It's Unlike Anything We'd Ever Expected

"A Wasteland Full of Cats, a Fallout-inspired adventure!"

In and amongst all of the GTA 6 news that's been happening this week, Bethesda has made a very quiet announcement about a new Fallout-inspired game, and it's one of the most bizarre crossovers we've seen in a while!

Simply put, Xbox and Bethesda are teaming up with the developers behind games such as A Building Full of Cats to create a Wasteland-themed game where you'll seemingly have to locate cats throughout the Fallout universe.

In other words, this would appear to be a hidden object game.

We'll throw some footage of one of this developer's Xbox titles down below so you can get an idea of what to expect. Their games are also always very inexpensive, and they also have some fantastic reviews on the Xbox Store.

There's obviously lots of other Fallout stuff in the works right now, including two remasters based on Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas, as well as the much-anticipated Fallout 5. This new "inspired" game clearly just serves as a bit of fun to plug the gap, and we reckon it might actually do very well when it launches in the future.

It's cool to see Xbox partnering on lighthearted ideas like this! Long may it continue - do it with Halo and Gears next?

#4096. Bandai Namco is liquidating Unknown 9: Awakening studio Reflector Entertainment, following multiple previous layoffs since the game's launch

As another addition to the slew of smaller studios being dissolved by their parent companies, Bandai Namco announced in a press release that they are shutting down their subsidiary studio Reflector Entertainment, a Montreal studio responsible for 2024's action-adventure game Unknown 9: Awakening. In its notice, Bandai Namco explains that the reason for the liquidation is due to Reflector not meeting its expectations for "future business plans, necessary additional investment, and the possibility of profitability and business continuation."

The press release notes that the liquidation of Reflector will result in an estimated "extraordinary loss" of around 21 million euros, or 3.5 billion yen, for Bandai Namco in its Q3 fiscal report of this year. This is not the first time Reflector has been cut by Bandai, as around a month after the launch of Unknown 9: Awakening and presumably in response to its low sales, 18% of the workforce was laid off. 2025 then saw further redundancies amidst the cancellation of a prospective project, though details on those layoffs were not granted by the company. Unknown 9 was intended to be a transmedia franchise involving the game as well as comic books and novels, but these ambitions never came to pass.

Bandai Namco notes that the liquidation will be held to local laws and procedures, which make the actual schedule of the process uncertain for now. A similar process faces Arkane Lyon, which is currently in a purgatory of having been chosen for closure by Microsoft, but temporarily protected by French labor laws that prevent it from being suddenly closed without proper negotiation and procedure.

Channing Tatum doesn't think his Gambit voice has changed, reminding fans that Avengers: Doomsday "is not Deadpool tone"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Contrary to what Marvel fans may think, Gambit star Channing Tatum says he hasn't toned down his mutant's accent in Avengers: Doomsday, it's just less Cajun French.

"I think I have been quoted in the press as toning down the accent. That is not exactly what I'm doing. I'm just speaking less Cajun French," said Tatum to Associated Press. "It's hard to explain, but basically Cajun French is French that almost French people can't understand. So I'm speaking less of that, but the Cajun accent is still there."

Tatum first took to the screen as Gambit in Deadpool and Wolverine, where he sported a rather thick accent. In Marvel comics, the hero, real name Remy LeBeau, does indeed speak with an Acadiana twang, reflecting his Louisiana heritage. However, fans were quick to point out the difference in Gambit's accent in the first listen at his voice ahead of Doomsday, which arrived earlier this month in a Dunkin Donuts commercial.

Nevertheless, Tatum reminds fans that Doomsday is a very different movie from Deadpool 3, which might explain his change in cadence. "The movie and the tone in general is not Deadpool tone. Shawn Levy and Ryan Reynolds have their own tone that is specific to the Deadpool movies," explained Tatum. "The Russos, they have comedy and levity in their movies, but they definitely will punch you in the gut emotionally as well. So I think you're going to get a lot more drama. There's going to be a lot of drama in the movie, let me just say that."

Though he couldn't give too much away, Tatum said we can "expect a little more emotional moments" from his mutant. "The movie is going to take you on a ride. We get to see a little bit more of Gambit's fighting style," added the star. We have already seen Gambit flick some cards at Shang-Chi in the Doomsday trailer, but the hero will have to learn to work as a team if he wants to defeat Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom as he threatens to destroy multiple Marvel timelines.

Gambit will be joined by other X-Men in the Marvel Phase 6 movie, including Patrick Stewart's Charles Xavier, Ian McKellen's Magneto, James Marsden's Cyclops, Alan Cumming's Nightcrawler, and Rebecca Romijn's Mystique.

Avengers: Doomsday hits cinemas on December 18, and December 16 in the UK. For more, check out our guide to the Marvel timeline, and keep up with upcoming Marvel movies and shows on the way.

#4093. Company of Heroes 3 developer admits "it was a lot" to make the 3.0 overhaul patch alongside regular updates, singleplayer DLC, and a whole spinoff game

The Company of Heroes 3's 3.0 update is huge. Touching virtually every part of the three-year-old RTS, the patch notes are longer than, well, my arm isn't a great measure of patch note length. Let's just say the headline features of overhauled VFX and audio don't really cover it. It also comes with new autumn and winter biomes, an updated grand strategy campaign, improvements to unit AI, and a whole host of other changes.

Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 update's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.

The team began planning the 3.0 update two years ago, seeing the series' 20th anniversary as an opportunity to make a significant update to Company of Heroes 3, and focus on issues players had flagged since launch. "The VFX were called out," executive producer Denise Christie tells me. "Same thing with a lot of our audio."

Relic were already releasing patches every three months, but the changes they were looking at were much too large for those smaller updates. If they had tried to do the work as part of the small updates, approaching the problems with piecemeal solutions, it would have turned Company of Heroes 3 into a hodgepodge of new and old assets. "We wanted to make sure it was a cohesive package," principal designer Eric Wrobel says. "If you increase the quality of one thing, you have to do it equally across so much stuff." Otherwise you end up with "One that looks awesome and one that's like, 'Oh, this one's kind of gross'."

Complicating matters, though, was that the team couldn't down tools and focus on just these large changes. As well as the small patches that were still going out every three months, both the VFX and audio teams were also contributing the battlegroup DLC packs which added new units to the game. "They would work on stuff and in one branch that was the 3.0 work and then they would go ahead and do some battlegroup stuff and come back to that," Christie says. "It was a lot."

As the 3.0 update grew in scope, it also meant other departments were contributing to the anniversary release while working on the smaller updates and DLC. "For us to create future maps for Company of Heroes 3, we were going to have an issue that our assets were getting stale," Christie explains. So, as part of 3.0, Relic's art department created autumn and winter asset packs, as well as a new Industrial theme. This then created more work for the VFX team, who have added rain and snow, as well as a transition effect showing soil and concrete moving from dry to wet.

Not to be outdone, the design team also made significant changes to the singleplayer Italy campaign. The towns that dot the dynamic grand strategy-inspired map now have individual upgrades, making for more meaningful decisions when it comes to which settlement you capture next. And, responding to one of the main criticisms of Company of Heroes 3's singleplayer, they also updated the computer's AI so it makes smarter decisions in both the turn-based and real-time battles. "We wanted to get this feel like there was that sort of back and forth of the AI resisting you and pushing forward into your territory and actually taking your stuff, which wasn't really happening in any of the previous updates," Wrobel says.

Further complicating matters was the fact that alongside these regular updates, the DLC, and the big 3.0 update release work, was that Relic also released Final Stand in July, a roguelike horde mode spinoff of Company of Heroes 3. "We had to be very careful not to accidentally introduce this 3.0 work that was also happening at the same time," Christie says." The improvements in this update have also rolled out for the spinoff, too.

Naturally, Relic aren't doing all this work purely out of the goodness of the hearts. The regular updates keep players engaged, Christie explains, and "hopefully bring back lapsed players who were frustrated by some of these things." It's something the team have already seen happen before, Wrobel explains. "We saw with the 2.0 update that we had a big spike of users and that was great, but because that improved the overall quality of the game, we saw each month we were selling more copies than we were before. People have been buying these games for years and years and years, so if we invest in this now we're going to see returns for quite a long time into the future as well."

"If we were starting to see that tail down then we probably would have made a very different decision to be honest, but that's not what we see," Christie adds.

The next release for Company of Heroes 3 is a singleplayer DLC, Operation Torch, due out on November 25th. (So, if you're keeping count, that was also in the works while the update, battlegroup DLC, and spinoff were all being made.) Until now, Relic's additions to the RTS have been focused on the multiplayer community, adding new units to be used online or in offline skirmishes. Operation Torch brings new scripted missions that trace a set of soldiers moving through North Africa.

After that, though, I ask if Relic plans to continue adding to Company of Heroes 3 or if they're ready to move onto a new project. "Well, it's both actually," CEO Justin Dowdeswell tells me. "We would love to continue with Company of Heroes 3 and not solely as a place for us to experiment. That's one of the advantages of being smaller, and being able to make decisions. We're not going to leave Company of Heroes 3. It's an and function. We are going to embark on the next thing."

So, it doesn't sound like Relic are taking anything off their plate…

#4092. Wolverine PS5's Sales Absolutely Plunged in October

Marvel’s Wolverine may have started strong in September’s Circana sales report, but it plunged in October.

Sony’s big PS5 exclusive for 2026, which attracted reasonable if utterly unremarkable reviews, ranked 14th in the latest US best-sellers list – dropping dramatically from first position the month of its release.

The game is now 15th overall for 2026 as a whole, down from 11th position in September. It’ll continue to fall with juggernauts like GTA 6 now officially out.

Couple other notes: Marvel's Wolverine dropped from 1st in Sept to 14th in Oct, ranks in top 15 YTD. On the YTD charts, less than $10M separates 8th place from 13th - it's a tight cluster.

The exclusive’s lore accurate lack of legs can likely be attributed to the game’s worse than expected reviews.

While it’s not universally disliked – we awarded it an 8/10, after all – fans understandably expect better from dev Insomniac.

Sony’s running discounts on the game during Black Friday to try and stimulate some enthusiasm around it, and I suspect this may be one of those titles that ends up in a lot of hardware bundles in the future.

To be fair, the platform holder seemed relatively satisfied with the title’s 2.4 million sales during its recent financial report.

I suppose it’s possible the launch numbers really did meet its expectations, but it may now be disappointed with the title’s long-term momentum – or lack thereof.

We’ll probably have to wait until its next investor update before we get more information.

There’s certainly some truth in that, and it’s always been the common wisdom. But I think the AAA market is a bit more complex now. Many of these big AAA games also get really long tail sales, they rely of that for making a lot of extra profit and getting people into the IP later.

Look at GoW: Ragnarok reportedly selling 20+ million units, yet only around 5 million were in the first week. Similar for Spider-man, Horizon, TLOU, GT7 and other big IP that keep selling long after release, they only hit those huge milestones from long tail sales. There was even an article on Bloodborne selling another 250k copies last year.

Of course not all sales are equal, financially day 1 sales will be at full price where as long tail sales will often be at a discount. And month 1 sales may also be used to judge a games success and make decisions for the studio going forward, they are still vital but don’t tell the whole story.

#4091. HDR Expert Shares Their Three Recommended Display Settings For GTA 6

The good (and hilarious) folks over at HDTVTest have been looking at the HDR Calibration settings for GTA 6 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and they've discovered that the tool is actually slightly broken as things stand.

Some of the specifics go over my head a little bit to be honest, but in a nutshell, the figures that are displayed on the calibration tool don't fully translate into the game itself, leading to a potentially inoptimal picture.

As a result, they've published a new nine-minute video (which you can see up above) to explain the issues.

"The HDR calibration screen in GTA 6 can be misleading, because Rockstar's Max Brightness, Paper White and Black Levels settings interact in unexpected ways. To be clear, GTA VI's HDR rendering isn't broken… it's the calibration procedure that can give misleading results."

The video goes step-by-step on how they analysed the issues and tried to figure out the best possible HDR settings for GTA 6, and while their tests aren't fully concluded yet (there's another video to come in the future where they try multiple consumer displays), they've shared their initial best settings for displays capable of 1,000 nits or brighter.

Here are those three settings, but again, keep in mind that your TV must be capable of 1,000 nits of brightness or more, and that certain smart TV features or special HDR settings on your TV itself may interfere with the results.

If your display isn't capable of 1,000 nits, do a bit of Googling to try and find out the specifics for your TV/monitor, and then times that figure by two in-game. So, if you're working with a maximum of 600 nits, set the figure as 1,200.

I have to be honest and say I'm not seeing a lot of difference here, but I've also got an old TV with a max brightness of just over 600 nits, not to mention I'm using a few image-altering features that may be playing havoc with the settings. It's also noted in the video that this is generally based on playing in the dark, rather than in a brightly-lit room.

Have a play for yourself and see what you think - there's clearly a lot of people who are very thankful for these settings on YouTube and beyond, so we wanted to at least make you aware of them. The reality is that you may need to still do a bit of tweaking to find the perfect sweet spot for your setup though.

#4090. Nvidia shareholders have filed a lawsuit against the tech company over claims that they were misled regarding CEO Jensen Huang's affair

If I wasn't so sick of hearing about AI every day of my life at the moment I might have found it funny to hear that one of the biggest peddlers of the poison around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was caught having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Oh who am I kidding, it is funny! And despite knowing that this won't likely push Nvidia away from AI, I am a bit tickled to hear that the tech company and Huang are on the receiving end of a lawsuit.

The suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm. Kistenmacher is an Nvidia shareholder, and with this suit he's seeking to "recover compensable damages," for himself and other shareholders due to the "precipitous decline in the market value of the Company’s securities." What a palaver! I do not imagine this will be resolved particularly quickly.

As it currently stands, Huang has only admitted to having an affair rather than any trade secrets being leaked anywhere. Nvidia had this to say on the matter: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate."

The concern comes from the person Huang had an affair with, one Alice Huang (no, they aren't related), a former managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company who have allegedly given Chinese companies Nvidia chips they bought billions of US dollars of. A messy situation to be sure, and one I unconfidently hope brings about the end of AI, somehow.

#4087. Marathon is becoming a whole new game next month with a roguelite PvE mode, a beta for a very Halo-esque team deathmatch mode, a vibey social space and more

Marathon is getting a lot bigger next month. In September, Bungie outlined their plans for the shooter making some big promises, namely the arrival of a PvE mode, and now they've shown off what you can expect from its next season, Symbiosis.

Top of the order is that PvE mode, which has a name now: Expedition. It's a roguelite mode, one that's playable in co-op, though a lack of details at this current time doesn't make it clear as to whether you can run it solo or not. The season's trailer, which you can have a gander at below, gives off the impression that you'll have to complete particular tasks before exfiltrating like you normally do. I'm sure we'll learn more in time.

The previously promised social space will be coming with this update too, and it's called Limbo. Morbidly appropriate! You can hang out here with your buds, head to a mini arena for some impromptu matches (I think), or head to the firing range where you can test out your weapons. You'll also be able to try out the new runner shell, Bishop, a cooler than you, samurai-sword-wielding robot who can jump real good and do that cool movie thing where it slices a whole bunch of enemies at once in one swing real quick like.

What will undoubtedly have some folks going "Halo's back!" is the beginning of a beta test for a team deathmatch mode. The Halo comparison is apt not simply because of the fact that it's Bungie who are making it, but because there's a deep-voiced announcer guy talking about all the sick kills you do. Details are slim on how this will work too. Beyond that, there's a few new weapons to flaunt, and maybe most excitingly, big ole alien enemies to take on.

You've still got a little while to wait for Symbiosis, which is currently slated to launch on December 8th. The game will be free to play from then until December 15th, too, obviously in a bid to show sceptics how good it is now (hopefully it is good, for Bungie's sake).

#4086. Ahead of GTA 6 and as concerns over genAI PC ports grow, Take-Two's CEO says they're revving up their "technical defences" and "legal activites" over piracy

"[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that"

It's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey? A bad time, obviously, as it's infecting everything from game development, to the modding community, to native PC ports of a remake of a very popular game that I won't link to for fear of a certain company finding out where I live and ending me there and then. And of course, the latter may be a concern for one Rockstar Games and the impending release of GTA 6. But according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, game's publisher, they are currently technically and legally preparing themselves.

IGN recently spoke to Zelnick regarding potential AI cloning concerns, notably about any business issues they may face as a result. "I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business," Zelnick explained. "I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended."

Zelnick also made a comment about thinking "all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," in response to a question about whether he wants to see OpenAI follow in Claude's footsteps by limiting the potential for genAI clones. "If you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he said.

It was during an investor Q&A where Zelnick dug into the precautions Take-Two are take-twoing in regards to the growing threat of AI. "[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it."

Essentially: unless you want to face the wrath of the kinds of lawyers multi-billion dollar companies can afford, I wouldn't bother trying to clone GTA 6 with AI! Probably won't end well!

#4084. Simu Liu explains where Shang-Chi has been this whole time in the MCU, and it actually makes a lot of sense

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Get the biggest gaming news, reviews, and releases straight to your inbox.

Bringing all the latest movie news, features, and reviews to your inbox

Unlock instant access to exclusive member features.

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

It's been 5 years since we've seen Shang-Chi in the MCU

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Shang-Chi first debuted in 2021's Shang Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, but as was recently teased by Marvel, we haven't really heard from him since. The character is now set to return to the MCU in Avengers: Doomsday, where he'll team up in the fight against Doctor Doom.

It's not clear if his absence will be addressed in the upcoming superhero movie, but in a new interview, actor Simu Liu has shared his head canon about where his character has been this whole time, and it actually makes a lot of sense.

Appearing on the Countdown to Doomsday podcast, Liu was asked about what he thinks Shang-Chi has been up to. After some discussion about how he's definitely been fired from his job, Liu shared an insight into his character's backstory.

"I actually think that he's much more likely to go back to Ta Lo," he told the hosts, referencing the gorgeous mystical realm that his characters visits in his movie. "Just because he experiences for such a short period of time before stuff starts to go haywire. But it's really that peace of just remembering what it was like to drive through that for the first time, the experience of the animals but also to reconnect with his aunt and his family, I imagine that's probably really powerful for him."

Liu went on to add that his return may also come "from a place of humility" as "he's just gotten these rings and he has no idea really how to use them." In Liu's mind, he got lucky in the movie's final fight, and ended up channeling the skills of his parents. "I think maybe there was some realization that he had to go and hone his powers still," he added.

Well, it looks like he's mastered them now from what we've seen in the Avengers: Doomsday trailers so far. He's set to face Gambit at some point too, which Liu compared to his iconic bus fight in Shang Chi and the Legend of the 10 Rings in an interview with Empire.

If you're hoping to catch up before the release of Avengers: Doomsday, check out our Road to Doomsday series as well as our guide the Marvel timeline so far.

#4083. Sony have cancelled Fairgame$, once again reminding us that chasing live service big bucks basically never works

You know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

This comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony said that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

Bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

Sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

For those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was announced back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a new name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

#4082. Talking Point: How Often Are You Willing To Play Games At 30FPS?

While GTA 6 has been receiving unbelievable praise and is technically considered one of the best video games of all time according to Metacritic, that certainly doesn't mean it's immune to criticism.

One of the big talking points both before and after launch has been that it's a 30FPS experience across all Xbox and PlayStation consoles, and if you're going from 60FPS back to 30FPS, there's definitely an adjustment period. Some people are absolutely fine with that, while others are finding it extremely difficult to go back.

For what it's worth, our friends at Digital Foundry have been analysing this in depth today:

Feature Why Isn't Grand Theft Auto 6 60fps?

Digital FoundryAnd could frame generation be the solution?

Rockstar Games has already confirmed recently that even the PS5 Pro doesn't come close to running GTA 6 at 60FPS due to the system's processor not being powerful enough, so we might be forced to wait until the next generation of consoles (and PC) before the game will become playable at 60 frames per-second.

"The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.”

With all of this in mind, we're interested to hear what you think about playing games at 30FPS on Xbox, PlayStation or anywhere else. It's becoming much more common that 60FPS is the default these days, but there are still some phenomenal 30FPS-only experiences out there, and it's a shame to think people are missing out on them.

I personally much prefer playing at 60FPS if I can, and there are certain games I will avoid at 30FPS until they get a patch down the line (like Mafia: Definitive Edition), but when it comes to industry-defining masterpieces like Red Dead Redemption 2 and Grand Theft Auto VI, the last thing I'd want is for them to scale back the detail in order to squeeze in a 60FPS mode.

#4081. Guide: GTA 6: Radio Songs - All Music, Radio Stations, & Artists

As with the previous games in the series, GTA 6 has a staggering amount of both licensed and original music. There's so much to listen to, whether it's selected tracks during key story moments or you're just driving around with the radio on. In this GTA 6 guide, we're going to tell you everything you need to know about GTA 6's music.

On this page: All Radio Songs and Artists in GTA 6

Below is a list of every radio song in the game, divided by where and how they appear throughout GTA 6.

French electronic duo Justice has composed and produced the original score for GTA 6, providing music that soundtracks the entire experience. Here's the track list:

GTA 6: The Album is a selection of 34 original tracks produced just for GTA 6. Many of these also play on certain radio stations, listed below. Here's the album's track list:

As is tradition in the GTA series, GTA 6 features many radio stations you can listen to while going about your business in Leonida. Here, we list each station, along with all the songs they play. Songs that are totally new for the game are highlighted in bold.

As well as the radio stations, GTA 6 includes a number of original podcast series to enjoy. Each one features multiple episodes to listen to, unlocking as you progress. Here they all are:

The radio and podcasts can be listened to in a number of ways in GTA 6.

The most obvious way is while driving. In any vehicle, if the radio isn't on already, hold Left and turn it on with Cross/X. You can scroll through stations with L1 and R1:

To access podcasts, move the right stick down:

Outside of vehicles, you can find radios dotted around the environment; you can toggle them on with Left and choose a station (you cannot listen to podcasts on a radio):

Another option is to use headphones or earbuds.

Electronics stores sell over-ear headphones and earbuds, which allow you to listen to radio stations and podcasts while you're on foot.

To find an electronics store, open the map with Touch Pad, then use the directional buttons to reach Style, then Electronics. Nearby shops will populate the list, and you can set a waypoint from there:

Once you've bought a pair, equip them by holding L1, pressing R1 to access your items, then highlighting Headgear and pressing Cross/X as shown:

Now, you will be able to select radio stations and podcasts just like when you're driving.

GTA 6 features numerous musical artists and other celebrities, making cameo appearances in the game. Here they all are:

That's it for our guide to the radio songs in GTA 6. What are your favourite tunes to listen to in the game? Tell us in the comments section below, and be sure to check out our GTA 6 guide for much more.

#4079. Sick BMX flips, colourful characters, a whole lot of mail and a charming raccoon dog await you in Tanuki: Pon's Summer, which you can pick up now

Right, today's been miserable thanks to the now hourly discourse we have to all take part in lest we be seen as approving of the current bad thing, how about something that looks simply pleasant? Today's the launch day for Tanuki: Pon's Summer, a delightfully vibrant mail delivery sim/Tony Hawk's Pro Skater but for bikes about restoring a shrine before the end of summer.

I've been enamoured by the vibe of Tanuki: Pon's Summer since it was announced in no small part because of how in some small ways it reminds me of Boku No Natsuyasumi, a cult-classic, Japan-only game series that's mostly just about hanging out in the Japanese countryside. This one isn't so lackadaisical, as you do have a job to do in delivering mail, but I think a similar spirit is there.

When it comes to delivering mail, there is a Death Strandingian element to it in your need to place your boxes on your BMX (which you can do sick tricks and flips on, of course) to maximise how much you can deliver. A bit less stressful than Kojima's joint, obviously, though elements are still there. Any money you earn from this gig can then be spent on restoring the shrine that you oh so love, which falls onto the sim side of things with the ability to fully customise how the shrine looks.

There are also a whole heap of minigames to perform that helps you get to know the locals. I'm talking baseball, sumo wrestling, working in a sushi restaurant and, of course, fishing. You can see bits of that in the launch trailer above, which comes with as 2010s an anime opening song you could wish for with some animation so good it makes me want an adaptation of the game. In time, perhaps! You can pick it up on Steam right here.

#4078. Despite IMAX being the best way to watch The Odyssey, Christopher Nolan explains what's "fun" about watching at home

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Get the biggest gaming news, reviews, and releases straight to your inbox.

Bringing all the latest movie news, features, and reviews to your inbox

Unlock instant access to exclusive member features.

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

Christopher Nolan reveals the benefits of watching The Odyssey at home

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

IMAX might be the best way to watch Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, but the director has shared the bright side of watching his Greek mythology epic at home, too.

"The fun thing about watching a film in the home is a different kind of concentration," Nolan told Polygon. "When you go to a movie, you're in the dark, you're really focused for a couple hours. In the home, it's a different type of concentration because you can pause the movie, you can go get a snack, come back."

As Nolan explains, at home, you can zero in on different elements. "It does allow you to control the timeline and really look at the detail of things," he added. "And for me, it's really about the performances."

Plus, the director encourages watching more than once. "The human element is what connects you with the story," he said. "But I think the work of these actors, this cast, this incredible cast in the film, it rewards multiple viewings."

The Odyssey's absolutely massive ensemble cast includes the likes of the new James Bond, Robert Pattinson, as well as Tom Holland, Matt Damon, Charlize Theron, Anne Hathaway, Jon Bernthal, and many more.

"There's subtleties and nuances in what they're doing that I, in the edit suite, get to watch again and again and again and sort of pick up on all the different things that Matt or Anne or Tom or Rob, what they're bringing to things, or Samantha Morton," Nolan continued. "It's really fun for people to be able to look at that in the home and see all the different layers that these guys have put into the story."

While you can watch the film at home, however, don't expect to see any deleted scenes. "There's a lot of deleted scenes scrumpled up in the wastebasket that no one will ever see," Nolan shared recently. "I don't really believe in director's cuts. I want to stand by the film that goes out. As a writer-director, I try to do a lot of that weeding out. There aren't many scenes that were shot."

The Odyssey is returning to IMAX 70mm this December if you missed it the first time around. With a current box office total of over $1.8 billion, it's the highest-grossing R-rated movie ever.

For more, check out our The Odyssey review, or our guide to all the most exciting upcoming movies.

#4077. GTA 6 Too Dark? Here's How to Fix It on PS5

Optimal HDR calibration settings included

If you’re playing GTA 6 and finding it too dark, there’s a good chance you may have your HDR calibration wrong – and no, it’s not your fault!

An extensive research video by HDTV Test – performed on a pricey Sony reference monitor – reveals the game’s HDR calibration may not be working quite as intended.

So while you may have followed the steps perfectly, setting your values until the Rockstar logo is only just visible as instructed, it may not be displaying optimally in your game.

I’d recommend you watch HDTV Test’s video for the full scientific analysis, but in short he explains that the various values in the HDR calibration settings output unexpectedly in-game.

Furthermore, the Rockstar release completely ignores Sony’s global PS5 HDR settings, so while you may have those calibrated perfectly for your particular screen, that won’t help you here.

Here’s how to fix it on PS5, according to HDTV Test – although do keep in mind your optimal personal settings will depend on your display, room, and preferred ambient lighting.

Load the game and press Options > Settings > Display > HDR Calibration.

HDTV Test recommends ignoring Rockstar’s own brightness calibration, so don’t worry too much if the company’s iconic logo is visible or not.

Instead focus on the two sample images of the party on the boat, which you can toggle between light and dark using R1.

These are the recommended starting settings for a display capable of 1,000 nits or higher:

Feel free to tune these to taste; your own optimal HDR calibration settings will depend on your environment and screen, after all.

But this should help with the overall appearance of the game, and ensure you’re able to see a little bit better in the dark.

#4076. Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO says – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Company of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Company of Heroes provides.

Dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell says. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio."

Just as a hint of the messy history of acquisitions and auctions: this year we see Dawn of War 4 coming from studio King Art Games and published by Deep Silver. Deep Silver are a subdivision of Plaion, formerly called Koch Media, which was acquired by Embracer Group back when they were called THQ Nordic. Not that they were actually the THQ that originally published Relic's Dawn of War, Nordic Games renamed themselves THQ Nordic after they bought the THQ trademark at auction.

As for Homeworld, Borderlands developer Gearbox picked up the license to the sci-fi RTS in the bankruptcy auction, then contracted Blackbird Interactive's support on the remasters, before handing the latter lead development on Homeworld 3. That chain of events does have a more clear throughline to Relic's past however, as Blackbird was created by two of Relic's co-founders Rob Cunningham and Jon Aaron Kambeitz. (Speaking of studios struggling without the series they made their name with, Blackbird was on the verge of bankruptcy before Gearbox got in touch with the Homeworld work. So we very nearly existed in a world where they never got to make the brilliant Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak and Hardspace Shipbreaker.)

None of this is intended to be a knock on Dawn of War 4. From what I've played it's a very good Warhammer 40K RTS, if it perhaps sticks a little closely to the model laid down by Relic's original. What do I know, though, talking about their own games, Dowdeswell tells me that while "one of the messages to the studio is we can't just make [the same] things that we made 20 years ago and hope it goes well", re-releasing the 20-year-old Dawn of War sold very well for Relic and netted the team some very positive reviews on Steam. "There's a bit of a paradox there," he adds"

Anyway, this is all getting side-tracked. Back to holding onto Company of Heroes when separating from Sega. "Fighting for Company of Heroes when leaving Sega was crucial because I already lamented the fact that the other games didn't come with Relic," Dowdeswell says. "I couldn't really imagine a Relic where none of the games that the studio has made and was known for were any longer part of it."

Relic and new owner UK investment firm Emona Capital LLP were able to negotiate Company of Heroes as part of the sale from Sega and since then the studio has spent the past two years focusing largely on supporting the WW2 RTS and restoring their back catalogue. The most recent update is the massive 3.0 patch to mark the series' 20th anniversary. Which, among many changes, overhauls the Mediterranean-set RTS game's special effects, audio systems, NPC AI, and makes significant changes to the singleplayer grand strategy-inspired Italy campaign, as well as adding a whole set of autumn and winter-themed assets for community map makers. They've also released a series of DLCs adding new factions to Company of Heroes 3's skirmishes and multiplayer, re-released Dawn of War with a definitive edition and announced they're doing the same for the original Company of Heroes, along with Blackbird Interactive's help. Dowdeswell says foundation building masks a lot of the work going on behind the scenes: "We now self-publish all of this," he explains. "There were a number of things that we had to learn, skills we had to develop, capacity and capability that we had to build at the studio very, very quickly."

I ask if it was always the plan to focus on their back catalogue, or if they had plans to release new games. Dowdeswell says spending four years quietly working on a new game wasn't an option: "It's almost impossible to do it that way because of the current climate in the industry. We don't have a financial safety net." Though, the team do have larger ambitions. "We want to make new games, we want to provide a modern Relic game," Dowdeswell says. "That ambition to re-establish Relic as an innovator in this strategy space is a big part of what drives our creative direction on new games." Focusing on updating Company of Heroes 3, releasing DLC for the game, and making definitive editions of Dawn of War and the original Company of Heroes is what gets the studio to the place it can make a new game.

However, Dowdeswell resists any framing of Relic's work on Company of Heroes 3 as spinning their wheels or resting on their laurels while working toward a new game. He argues the game "sits in between" Relic's past and its future: "It's an established game that came out three years ago, but it's also a way for us to take some chances, experiment a little bit, and while doing that staying really closely connected to the players, That's what the idea was behind the updates because it was a way to have very quick iterations and touch points with players and provide, honestly, a way for us to fund everything in the future."

As to what Relic is making next, Dowdeswell wouldn't say. Though, he revealed trying genres besides real-time strategy was "almost a certainty", before adding "I don't think it's going to be a vast departure for where we are, so it will still be strategic gameplay. We're not going to go build a racer."

#4075. Professor Layton and the New World of Steam digital pre-orders now available for Switch 2 and Switch, story and gameplay detailed

Following last week‘s PlayStation 5 and PC pre-order launch, Switch 2 and Switch digital pre-orders for Professor Layton and the New World of Steam are now available for $64.99 / £53.99 / €64.99 / ¥7,920, LEVEL-5 announced. The official website has also been updated with story and gameplay information.

As previously announced, pre-orders include the “Layton Series Soundtrack Selection,” a digital soundtrack featuring 11 pieces of music from the Professor Layton series. The tracks are accessible via the “Secret Content” menu in-game.

This new adventure takes place one year after the events of Professor Layton and the Unwound Future.

The story unfolds in America, where the Wild West era has ended and the country is forging ahead into a new age of development.

A letter from Luke leads Layton to Steam Bison, a town renowned for its inventions…

Steam Bison has undergone rapid technological advances thanks to the steam engine. But mysterious events are unfolding one after another, from a phantom gunman who has kidnapped a wealthy heiress to a gang of zombies threatening the town. Layton and Luke join forces once again to investigate these strange occurrences and embark on a grand puzzle-solving adventure.

◆ A Story That Unfolds as You Solve Puzzles

You’ll encounter all kinds of puzzles as you explore the streets of Steam Bison.

—Even to meet Eggmuffin, an inventor, you’ll need to solve a puzzle to find the entrance to his room…

—Solve the puzzle, and the story moves forward.

Layton and Luke face more puzzles than ever before in the series. Solve a wide variety of puzzles as you progress through the story and get to the bottom of the mysterious events unfolding in Steam Bison. Along the way, you’ll even come across puzzles that play a part in Steam Bison’s development. Solve them to upgrade the town’s facilities and watch the town flourish.

What’s more, a new puzzle will be added to Daily Puzzles every day for over a year following launch. This lets you enjoy the game long after you’ve completed the story.

Whether you prefer to take your time solving puzzles on your own or gather around a big screen with family and friends to work them out together, that’s all part of the fun of the Layton series.

Stand Use snippets of conversation between café customers to recreate the drinks they ordered. Get the drinks right, and you might hear some juicy local gossip!

Use a mysterious device to transform ordinary items into treasure. Master its three modes: Reversal, Evolution, and Fusion!

The duck robot that monitors the factory won’t stop once it’s set in motion! Give it the right commands to overcome obstacles and complete the operational test.

Experience Professor Layton and the New World of Steam in different languages! Choose your preferred languages for text and voice, and set off on an adventure with Professor Layton and Luke! Mix and match languages to experience the story in a whole new way!

Explore the Professor Layton games in the order their stories take place.

Professor Layton and the New World of Steam is due out for PlayStation 5, Switch 2, Switch, and PC via Steam on December 10.

GTA 6 hasn't been out in the wild for long, but players are quickly discovering that our return to Vice City includes plenty of cameos – including a former Grand Theft Auto protagonist who really steals some scenes.

If the intro didn't give it away, we're headed for spoiler territory, so feel free to exit now if you're trying to keep GTA 6 a mystery.

Still here? Grand. I won't get too deep into story spoiler territory, though to recap enough to make sense of the various spoilers doing the rounds on the internet: GTA 6 eventually tosses protagonists Jason and Lucia into some dirty work with a wealthy shipping magnate who has ties to Eastern European criminals. That's your first hint.

Eventually, something goes wrong enough for a familiar face to get involved. That's right, GTA 6 does feature Niko Bellic of Grand Theft Auto 4 fame. Enough has been spoiled online, so I'll let you enjoy that for yourself, cousin. Or you could watch it all on YouTube, if you really can't wait.

Suspicions were first raised yesterday when Rockstar revealed the GTA 6 voice acting cast. Niko Bellic's name wasn't there, because spoilers, but actor Michael Hollick sure was. He's just down as The Hitman, so it could have been a nifty Easter egg, but alas – fans already have full playthroughs online, so you know the information was easy to find.

It's a lovely moment in truth. Behind the scenes, there have been plenty of reports that Hollick and Rockstar weren't on the best of terms over GTA 4's pay, given how much the game would go on to make. That said, time appears to heal all wounds. Over the years, Hollick has appeared more willing to engage with the GTA fandom – and now, a lovely little cameo moment.

#4073. Casualties: Unknown is a total pain simulator that makes other survival games seem like massive cowards

Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.

You haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics. This is an intricate and imaginative celebration of pain - not merely an exacting survival game full of gauges to manage, but a laboratory study of just how many ways an animal body can feel, before it finally gives up the ghost.

I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks. I am the sorrowing vat-grown pup of a conclave of star-faring Dr Moreaus. My task is to collect... something, some gadget of great importance, from a cave on a deathly planet, located beneath three kilometres of booby-trapped and infested, poisonous and hateful rock.

Currently, I am trying to burrow into a sealed titanium drop pod with my bare paws, so that I can sleep somewhere warm. Too warm, in fact. The drop pod heaters feel like they were vindictively designed to discourage occupants from lingering, but I'm finding that dehydration is easier to address than hypothermia - there are pools of groundwater around that harbour only a slight risk of "minorly" fouling my intestines. So into the pod we go. After ripping away a layer of rubber, I smash some glass panes and promptly step in the fragments.

My computer screams, a hideous jangle of chords and static. The interface becomes a fritzing, flexing sphincter of pinks and reds. My punctured dogsbody flops and writhes, spurting yellow fluids and gobs of unintelligible text, ignoring my button inputs. They are my avatar no longer. They have been reduced to a squirming facet of the simulation's agony.

I gawp in guilt and terror at the status bar, now jammed with pulsing icons, then switch to my health display and determine that I am "bleeding catastrophically" from my right hind paw. I need to bandage that paw quickly. But first, I need to remove the glass. This takes the form of a 'minigame' in which I guide a shaking clawed hand with the cursor, hauling out shards even as my poor character threatens to pass out from the ordeal.

I've got two of five shards out when the earthquake kicks in. Already doubled over and delirious, my pioneering pooch is launched over the nearest cliff. They fall about 50 feet, rag-dolling off crags with a concussive whump, till they smash into a flooded wooden platform. The anatomical diagram on the health screen lights up like a wickerman. I don't appear to have broken any bones, but everything is hurting. What's more, I am soaking wet and hypothermia is taking hold, stretching blue veins through the clenching colours of my pain. The screen begins to look like some exotic, putrid flower.

Wringing my hands, I allow my mutant mutt about 10 seconds to recover from the shock of the fall, then open the health screen again and slowly tug out the last three shards of glass. It's actually easier than before, but not for the happiest of reasons: landing on my head appears to have numbed my senses. There will be longer term consequences, probably. Now I just have to bind the wound… except that I must have dropped my roll of gauze, while tumbling through the abyss. With sirens still flashing on the HUD, I peer about for a cave plant or other source of crafting materials. On the other side of the platform, I spy the corpse of another pitiful lab experiment. Perhaps there's a bandage in that huddle of clothes?

I hoist my sagging and babbling starpup to their feet, and limp over to investigate. Then I step on a pressure plate, and a six foot blade shoots up through my left thigh.

The screen is almost obliterated by crimson snow. The noise is... indescribable. I open the health screen again to assess the damage but I can't, because my dogperson has fallen into utter derangement. They want to be rid of their too-fruitful arteries, their stinking yellow blood. The clawed hand reappears, and I am forced to rake my own torso with it to regain access to the controls.

I am now gushing my life out from head to foot. Going by my plummeting heart rate, I have about 30 seconds to burn before I lose consciousness forever. I see no means of recovery, and I can't bear to watch my character bleed out. So instead, I detonate the chip embedded in their brain - the same chip responsible for the interface's rash of icons and warnings. According to the subsequent mission report print-out, my canine pioneer was feeling "dejected" when their head exploded.

The worst thing about the scenario I've just recalled is that it represents Casualties: Unknown at its least punishing. All of the above took place in the first of the game's 11 biomes - each procedurally generated, and 300 metres high - on the default "Tough" run setting. Resources are more plentiful up here, while active threats are fewer. There is scope to faff about and prepare - gathering plant matter for a crude woven bag, so I don't have to carry everything in my hands or mouth or tuck it into the folds of my body. There is time to crack open supply crates, and craft an implement of some kind.

The main danger, traps aside, is falling. Casualties: Unknown's terrain generator is not your pal. As regards the opening couple of biomes, at least, it works like a broken muck spreader, ejecting a mix of filthy clogs and particles that snag your jumps and often oblige you to dig through rock and gravel. You'll frequently be doing that in the dark, and even the smallest of exertions takes a perceptible toll – whimpers of effort, wheezing breath, double vision. The one major consolation is that you can wall-jump and slide down surfaces, a mocking touch of Prince of Persia.

Still, further down is where life gets truly unpleasant. There are sonic traps in certain biomes that cause brain damage and massive hemorrhaging. There are vast, rumbling insects you simply cannot afford to get close to, because they are guaranteed to bite off a limb. And the absolutely dreadful thing about that is that it won't necessarily end your run: given a tourniquet and antibiotics, you may yet pull through. Perhaps you'll find or craft a prosthetic. The game's characters are, in general, astonishingly tough for all their immense capacity for anguish.

Casualties: Unknown is a brilliant and unusual piece of design, uninhibited by any commercialised and sanitary notions of 'fun' and 'difficulty'. It's committed to recreating the surge of sensation through flesh. There's something intrinsically vital about this. Like Project Citadel, perhaps, its extravaganzas of torment are about feeling more present and alive in a twisted world, more in control. I'm not the writer to discuss this, and I know little about the developer's circumstances, but it feels like an exploration of trans survival in the face of a brutalising biopolitical regime: the online wiki notes that the game's zoomorphic Experiments or "Expies" have their own ideas about gender, though I'm finding it tricky to distinguish those accounts from the categorisations of the evidently unfriendly boffins who engineered them.

I would like to get to the bottom of things. I would like to find that goddamn gadget. I would like to return to the surface and massacre the bastards who sent me down here. Still, I'm not sure I have the willpower to witness everything my avatar might have to endure: barotrauma, sepsis, strokes, ruptured ears, hallucinations... As I've hopefully made clear throughout this piece, it remains an open question as to whether I am them, or simply one of their human tormentors. You can read more on Steam and Itch.

#4072. 'It's Unbelievably Hard to Achieve': Cyberpunk 2077 Boss Pours Praise on 'Masterpiece' GTA 6

From Night City to Vice City, the boss of CDPR has nothing but nice things to say about GTA 6.

With the PS5 release of Cyberpunk 2077, the Polish studio established itself as an open world big boy, having previously released one of the greatest RPGs ever in The Witcher 3.

And so it’s only fitting for co-CEO Michal Nowakowski to pour praise on Rockstar’s latest release, now the highest rated game of all time.

“Rockstar Games created a masterpiece that I am planning to explore in the coming weeks and months. Massive congratulations to the whole team who worked on the game. It is unbelievably hard to achieve what you just did. Hats off to all of you.”

I personally believe it’s going to take years, if not decades, to surpass GTA 6.

The sheer density of the open world, from its dizzying array of art assets to the complexity of its sandbox simulation, is just in another universe to everything else.

Even if you’re not enjoying the game, it’s hard to argue against the standards being set here.

Of course, a high bar will raise the levels of absolutely everyone. I personally can’t wait to see what CDPR delivers with The Witcher 4 and its next Cyberpunk game.

Guide GTA 6 Guide: All Guides & Collectibles

#4071. As The Elder Scrolls 5 turns 15, massive mod Beyond Skyrim: Bruma gets a 2.0 update delivering a new quest, extra dungeons and an "expanded worldspace"

"The reason for this update is actually a technical necessity"

Warning: I'm probably about to make you feel old. Today, November 11th 2026, is the 15th anniversary of Skyrim's release. The first one, before it was re-released on every other platform under the sun. Fittingly, one of its best expansion mods, Beyond Skyrim: Bruma, has gotten a beefy 2.0 update to commemorate the occasion. Though, its creators insist the main driving force behind the update was more a matter of "technical necessity". There are new quests, dungeons, and corners of Skyrim-era Cyrodiil to explore either way.

"You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding new content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 update. "We are, of course, working on the whole province of Cyrodiil, and have made significant progress which you can follow on our social media. With so much still to go however, it was not out of nostalgia for a 15 year old Skyrim or a nearly 10 year old Bruma that we decided to revisit the first, and as of the time of writing, only major Beyond Skyrim release.

"The reason for this update is actually a technical necessity," the modders continued. "The problem we have with Bruma is that it is based on a very very old version of Cyrodiil, which had been branched off of the main development build of Cyrodiil soon after Bruma's initial release in 2017. Whenever we updated Bruma, that meant we had to merge our changes into two builds, the public Bruma build and the WIP Cyrodiil build." So, in order to solve that behind-the-scenes problem, the team have developed a "build stripper" tool which means they'll not have to juggle maintaining two builds going forwards.

As laid out in the showcase video above, the modders have also used Bruma 2.0 as an opportunity to overhaul and add to vast chunks of their recreation of Cyrodiil's northernmost county. A fully voiced quest called All The Wrong Places which was cut from the mod's initial release, "several new dungeons and interiors", and an expansion of the explorable area all grace the changelog.

More clothing, armour, weapons including the mod's first spear, enemies, spells, enchantments, world encounters, books, and treasure maps have also been shipped in with the 2.0 version, alongside overhauls to boss fights. A new opening title splash will greet you upon entering Bruma for the first time, you should benefit from higher FPS as you explore the city, and the modders have even added an apple to Jerall View Inn. That's far from the end of the tweaks, so it's well worth reading the full list if you've got time.

"All in all, Bruma 2.0 has been a massive journey, one where we have built and learned a lot, and most importantly, made many advancements to prepare us for the future," the modders concluded. If you've not given Beyond Skyrim: Bruma a go, I can very much recommend it. You might find yourself wandering back across the border into Skyrim once you've had your fill of nostalgia-tinged exploration and staring at a distant Imperial City you can't visit, but the original version's still good for hours of extra Elder Scrollsing.

You can grab the 2.0 version of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma from Nexus Mods. It's worth noting that you'll need "a recent version (1.6 or higher) of Skyrim: Special Edition's update.esm and update.bsa" and a separate mod containing Beyond Skyrim's shared asset repository. Saves made using previous versions of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma won't work with the 2.0 update, so it's likely worth starting a new playthrough or relying on an in-progress one you've yet to use any mods with.

#4070. Ubisoft lays off 166 staff at Montreal and Quebec studios

Ubisoft has laid off 166 staff across its Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec studios, the company announced.

“Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montreal and Quebec City operations,” a Ubisoft spokesperson said in a statement. “As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.”

The spokesperson continued, “We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognize the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.”

A source told IGN that the layoffs affect employees whose projects have been canceled or refocused, as well as those who could not be reassigned due to the decrease in the number of active projects.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 is without a doubt already proving successful, sitting as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic – but this quick success and its massive earning estimates aren't enough to curb fears of further layoffs at Rockstar Games.

The developers have spoken out about these concerns, with animation programmer Nestor Uriarte admitting he's "worried about getting laid off" even after "working on the biggest game of all time" – you know, Grand Theft Auto 6. Finance experts like Square Enix veteran Jacob Novak also stated the game's success indeed isn't enough to stop layoffs, as Rockstar has "built the biggest, most expensive game of all time and now released it."

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has something to say on the matter, too, sharing her thoughts over on Instagram. "99 Metacritic score. Multiple award nominations before it even released. Massive sales and player engagement. Incredible amounts of tangible and intangible value creation," she writes. "Yet the team is worried about layoffs. So, who receives the lion's share of the profits from their labor?"

Sadly, as Svedberg-Yen describes, "Not the vast majority of the creative team. One of the issues that happens when people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value. In finance, we call that value extraction." With this effect in mind – one I'd argue we've unfortunately seen a good bit of over the past few years within the video game industry – she hopes that Rockstar can successfully unionize."I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing," the writer concludes. "Layoffs during lulls in development cycles would work a lot better if teams were properly paid for the value they create, not just one-time, but throughout the life of the thing they created." While that's certainly true, it's unfortunately not always the reality – and that's precisely why Svedberg-Yen is rooting for unionization.

Just a day or so ago, she detailed how the industry "is eating itself" amid layoffs and studio closures, saying, "A lot of what's happening really breaks my heart." It's hard to not let it break your heart, honestly, as, again, it's not just Rockstar. We've reported on layoffs across various companies over recent years, ranging from Microsoft's plans to cut 3,200 employees at Xbox to BioWare's closure following the EA buyout.

Here's hoping that everyone lands on their feet at the end of it all – and that studios take notes from the likes of Nintendo's late president Satoru Iwata, who wisely said "employees who fear that they may be laid off" will never produce the same results as those who don't.

Check our GTA 6 review to see what we feel about one of the biggest new games this year, or browse through our handy GTA 6 guide for even more about Rockstar's huge release.
